gillnet.context: A rectangular wall of net with a grid of mesh, a row of floats on top and small weights along the bottom. Used for commercial fishing, fishery rules and gear guides.

purse-seine.context: Top view of a ring of net around a few fish, with a small boat beside it pulling the net closed. Used for tuna and sardine fishing, sustainable seafood and fishing method guides.

purse-seiner.context: Side view of a fishing boat with a tall mast, a slanted boom and a hanging pulley block. Used for industrial fishing fleets, tuna boats and fishery reports.

crab-boat.context: Side view of a fishing boat with a wheelhouse at the front and a tall stack of square cage pots on the back deck. Used for crab season, seafood sourcing and fishing trips.

dory.context: Side view of a small flat bottomed rowing boat with high flared sides, resting on a wavy line of water. Used for rowing, traditional fishing and small boat rentals.

glass-fishing-float.context: A round glass ball held in a diamond mesh of rope with a small loop on top. Used for seaside decor, beach finds and traditional net floats.

fish-box.context: An open crate packed with ice, with several forked fish tails sticking up over its rim. Used for fish markets, catch deliveries and seafood supply.

gaff-hook.context: A long straight pole ending in a large curved hook with a sharp point. Used in big game fishing to land a fish at the boat side.

harpoon.context: A long shaft with a barbed arrow head at one end and a ring of rope tied near the other. Used for whaling history, spear fishing and hunting gear.

netting-needle.context: A flat pointed shuttle with a center tongue and a notched tail, loaded with twine for tying fishing nets. Used for net making, net mending and craft guides.

trawl-door.context: A curved steel plate with a two legged chain and a towing wire running to a ring. Used in trawl fishing to spread the net mouth open.

squid-jig.context: A slim torpedo shaped lure with an eye and a crown of curved hooks around its lower end. Used for squid and cuttlefish fishing.

fighting-chair.context: A swiveling boat chair with a tall back, a footrest bar and a small rod socket at the front of the seat. Used for big game sport fishing charters.

fish-weir.context: Top view of a heart shaped fence of stakes standing in the water with a fish inside. Used for traditional tidal fish traps and fishing heritage.

net-drum.context: A large horizontal reel with a wide flange at each end, wound with fishing net, standing on a deck. Used on trawlers to store and haul the net.

cantilever-fishing-net.context: A square net hung on four ropes from a long wooden boom that leans out over the water from a shore post, with a counterweight at the other end. Used for traditional lift net fishing.

stilt-fishing.context: A fisher sitting on a small crossbar atop a single pole planted in the sea, holding a rod with its line dropped into the water. Used for Sri Lankan coastal fishing and travel content.

cormorant-fishing.context: A narrow boat with a lantern on a pole at the bow and a cormorant perched on its side. Used for traditional river fishing with trained birds and travel content.

fish-drying-rack.context: A wooden A frame with two crossbars and split fish hanging from them to dry in the air. Used for stockfish, dried fish and food preservation.

squid-fishing-boat.context: A fishing boat with a row of large round lamps hanging from a wire above the deck, used to lure squid at night. Used for night fishing and Asian coastal fleets.

handline-frame.context: An H shaped wooden winder wrapped with fishing line, with a sinker hanging from one end and a hook from the other. Used for simple hand line fishing and angling basics.

cutlass.context: A short curved sword with a wide single edged blade, a bowl shaped hand guard and a round pommel. Used for pirate themes, naval history and costumes.

doubloon.context: An old gold coin with a slightly uneven edge and a cross stamped in the middle. Used for pirate treasure, loot and game currency.

scrimshaw.context: A curved whale tooth with a tiny sailing ship engraved on its face. Used for sailor folk art, whaling history and museum collections.

sailors-valentine.context: An octagonal wooden box with a heart made of tiny seashells in the middle. Used for seashell crafts, keepsakes and romantic nautical gifts.

caulking-iron.context: A wide flat chisel with a flared cutting edge standing beside a round headed wooden mallet. Used for wooden boat building and sealing hull seams.

hardtack.context: A square ship's biscuit with a neat grid of small holes pricked across it. Used for sailor food history, survival rations and historical cooking.

widows-walk.context: A house with a small railed platform on top of its roof for watching the sea. Used for coastal homes, New England architecture and captain's houses.

crossed-anchors.context: Two anchors crossed diagonally over each other in an X. Used as a naval badge, a maritime crest or a harbor emblem.

fouled-anchor.context: An anchor with a rope wound loosely around its shank. Used as a classic navy emblem, sailor tattoo art and maritime logos.

powder-keg.context: A small barrel with metal bands and a lit fuse coming out of the top. Used for pirate and explosive themes, danger warnings and game items.

rolling-hitch.context: A vertical pole with a rope wrapped diagonally around it several times and a tail leaving at the top. Used for knot guides, sailing and scouting skills.

ghost-ship.context: An old sailing ship with torn, ragged sails and a jagged hull, with mist drifting beneath it. Used for haunted sea legends, Halloween and pirate games.

dive-lift-bag.context: An open bottomed bag of air rising underwater, lifting a small box on two straps below it. Used for salvage diving, underwater recovery and dive training.

oyster-tongs.context: Two long handles crossed at a pivot, with open toothed baskets at their lower ends. Used for gathering oysters from shallow beds and for oyster harvest guides.

push-net.context: A triangular net on two poles pushed through shallow water by a wading figure. Used for shrimping, small scale fishing and coastal livelihoods.

leeboard.context: Side view of a flat hulled barge with a large fan shaped board hinged to its flank and dipping below the hull. Used for historic sailing barges and sailing boat parts.

backstaff.context: An old navigation instrument with a long staff and two nested arcs of different sizes, with small sighting vanes. Used for maritime history and celestial navigation.

nocturnal-star-dial.context: A round dial on a short grip with a sighting hole at its center and a long pointer arm pivoting across it. Used to tell the hour at night from the stars.

marine-loading-arm.context: A jointed pipe arm folded like an elbow on a jetty, reaching across to connect to the deck of a tanker ship. Used for oil and gas terminals and cargo transfer.

vessel-traffic-tower.context: A tall harbor control tower with a wide glass walled room at the top and a radar bar turning above it. Used for port control, ship traffic monitoring and coastal safety.

faith-hope-charity-symbol.context: An emblem of a cross at the top, a heart in the middle and an anchor below, all on one vertical shaft. Used for religious jewelry, charms and maritime faith symbols.

rope-frame.context: A round frame made of thick twisted rope, its ends tied in a small knot at the bottom. Used for nautical decor, borders and wreath style frames.

rigid-inflatable-boat.context: Side view of a boat with a thick inflatable tube around a hard hull, a small console and an outboard motor on the back. Used for sea rescue, patrols and fast tenders.

sterndrive.context: Boat stern in side view with an engine hatch on the deck and a drive leg with a propeller bolted to the back of the hull. Used for power boat engines and marine propulsion.

ship-gunport.context: A square hatch in the side of a wooden ship's hull with its lid propped open and a cannon muzzle poking out. Used for warships, pirate ships and naval history.

deck-prism.context: A glass prism set flush in a ship's deck, flat on top and tapering to a point below, with light rays spreading underneath. Used for sailing ship details and daylight below decks.

quay-steps.context: Stone steps cut into a harbor wall running down into the water, with a small boat tied at the bottom. Used for waterfront landings and harbor access.

beach-seine.context: A curved wall of net in the shallows with a rope running from each end to figures hauling on the beach. Used for shore fishing and village fishing traditions.
